sndctrl.modname.tooltip: Enhances sound with reverb and occlusion.  Allows for control of how sounds are played.
sndctrl.cfg.sound.tooltip: General options for defining sound effects
sndctrl.cfg.sound.Occlusion.tooltip: Enable sound occlusion calculations (sound muffling when positioned behind blocks)
sndctrl.cfg.sound.StreamingSoundCount.to: Number of streaming sound channels to configure
sndctrl.cfg.sound.MonoConversion.tooltip: Enable conversion of stereo sounds to mono format for spacial play
sndctrl.cfg.sound.OccludeWeather.tooltip: Perform occlusion processing for sounds in the WEATHER category
sndctrl.cfg.sound.OccludeRecords.tooltip: Perform occlusion processing for sounds in the RECORDS category
sndctrl.cfg.sound.Individual.tooltip: Options to configure sounds on an individual basis
sndctrl.cfg.sound.StartupSounds.tooltip: Possible sounds to play when client reaches main game menu
sndctrl.cfg.sound.CullInterval.tooltip: Ticks between culled sound events (0 to disable culling)
sndctrl.cfg.sound.Threads.tooltip: Number of background threads to handle sound effect calculations (0 is default)
sndctrl.cfg.logging.tooltip: Defines how Sound Control logging will behave
sndctrl.cfg.logging.EnableDebug.tooltip: Enables/disables debug logging of the mod
sndctrl.cfg.logging.FlagMask.tooltip: Bitmask for toggling various debug traces
sndctrl.cfg.effects.Randoms.tooltip: Replace client side Randomizers with faster versions
sndctrl.cfg.effects.BlockRange.tooltip: Block range of entity special effect handling
sndctrl.text.quickvolumemenu.title: Quick Volume Settings
sndctrl.text.soundconfig.title: Individual Sound Configuration
sndctrl.text.soundconfig.cull.help: Marking a sound as CULL will limit the play to a single instance over a short period of time, reducing the overall load of the sound engine as well as ears.  Will only apply to sounds played through the Minecraft sound engine.
sndctrl.text.soundconfig.block.help: A sound marked as BLOCK will be prevented from playing.  Will only apply to sounds played through the Minecraft sound engine.
sndctrl.text.soundconfig.play.help: Plays the sound with the volume scaled by the volume scaling factor.  Does not apply any sound category volume modifiers.
sndctrl.text.soundconfig.volume.help: Set a volume scaling factor that gets applied when calculating the volume of a sound.  Increase to make quiet sounds louder; reduce to make loud sounds quieter.
sndctrl.configuration.title: Sound Control Configuration
sndctrl.cfg.sound.PlayerSounds2D.tooltip: Play your own water sounds (diving, swimming, splashing, water steps) in 2D: in stereo at the listener. Other players and mobs stay 3D
sndctrl.cfg.sound.PlayerSounds2DList.too: Sound ids that play in 2D when they come from yourself
sndctrl.cfg.sound.LoopCrossfade.tooltip: Make looping sounds (biome ambience, waterfalls) seamless: the silence at the start and end of the loop file is cut off and its end is crossfaded into its start, so you no longer hear where the loop restarts
sndctrl.cfg.sound.LoopCrossfadeLength.to: Length of the loop crossfade in milliseconds (at most a quarter of the loop is used). Applies to loops started after the change
sndctrl.cfg.sound.FadeInTime.tooltip: Milliseconds a positional loop (e.g. a waterfall) takes to fade in when it starts and to fade out when it stops (0 = start/stop at once)
sndctrl.cfg.sound.PanningSoftness.toolti: How much a sound exactly to your side is also heard on the other ear, as in real life. 0 = hard panning as in vanilla (100/0), 30 = 85/15, 60 = 70/30, 100 = both sides equal. Sounds in front and behind you are unchanged, distance and loudness stay the same. Only for normal stereo output; with Directional Audio (HRTF) or surround speakers it does nothing
